items.content_html:
Description

The accessibility notes on five animation-related pages share this sentence:

Additionally, certain kinds of motion can be a trigger for Vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine and Scotopic sensitivity.

The list has "and" twice, so it's hard to tell where one item ends and the next begins, and "Vestibular" and "Scotopic" are capitalized mid-sentence even though they're common nouns. The five copies have also drifted apart slightly. This makes them all read:

Additionally, certain kinds of motion can be a trigger for vestibular disorders, epilepsy, migraine, and scotopic sensitivity.

Page Before
Web Animations API Vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine, and Scotopic sensitivity
Using media queries for accessibility Vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine and Scotopic sensitivity
animation vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine and scotopic sensitivity
transition-timing-function Vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine and Scotopic sensitivity
<animate> Vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and migraine and Scotopic sensitivity

On transition-timing-function, the same sentence also joins two independent clauses with "and" but no comma ("…(ADHD) and certain kinds of motion can be…"), so it first reads as if "ADHD and certain kinds of motion" were one list. I added the comma there.

Motivation

The serial comma and the comma before "and" between two independent clauses both follow the writing style guide. Elsewhere on MDN, "vestibular disorders" is lowercase, and #43983 already lowercased the terms on the animation page.

Additional details

The sentence on the four CSS and SVG pages has been there since the initial import. The Web Animations API copy came in with #43469, moved from an older version on the Animation page.

I checked that no other page has this sentence. #45603 also touches transition-timing-function, but it adds a section above the Accessibility heading and doesn't change this paragraph.

Related issues and pull requests

  • #43983
  • #43469
items.title: Fix the list of conditions in the animation accessibility notes

items.content_html:
Description

Documents what happens in FedCM when the user isn't signed in to the IdP: in passive mode get() rejects, but in active mode (unless mediation is "silent") the browser opens the IdP's login_url in a dialog so the user can sign in, and then the flow continues.

Changes:

  • RP sign-in guide: the "Calling the get() method" section no longer says get() always rejects for logged-out users; it now explains the passive/active difference and links to the mode section.
  • RP sign-in guide, sign-in flow step 4: the note about all IdPs being logged out now covers active mode as well.
  • RP sign-in guide, "Active versus passive mode": takes out the wording that suggested users can enter IdP credentials in passive mode, and adds a paragraph explaining that the main practical difference is the IdP sign-in dialog for logged-out users. Also fixes the code sample, which had mode: active instead of mode: "active".
  • IdP integration guide, "How login status affects federated sign-in flow": mentions the active mode exception for the "logged-out" case.
  • IdentityCredentialRequestOptions: the active/passive value descriptions now say what happens when the user is not signed in.

Motivation

As the issue points out, a reader who wants to know whether a logged-out user can sign in to the IdP from get() would read the get() section, see that it rejects, and never find out that active mode exists mostly to handle this case.

Additional details

Spec: https://w3c-fedid.github.io/FedCM/#create-identity-credential, step 7.6 (if loginStatus is logged-out and mode is active and mediation is not "silent", fetch the config file and show an IdP login dialog).

I checked the changed files with markdownlint-cli2, prettier -c, and the front-matter linter, and built them with rari build, which reported no flaws. The new #login_url anchor resolves.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42136
items.title: FedCM: document that active mode lets logged-out users sign in to the IdP

items.content_html:
Description

The current text says that HTMLInputElement.labels is a NodeList, "if the element is not hidden", which is ambiguous, because it can be an element with the global "hidden" attribute or an input whose "type" is "hidden".

HTMLInputElement.labels is a NodeList when the global "hidden" attribute is set on the element.

Motivation

To fix an error.

Additional details

the labels IDL attribute of input elements, on getting, must return that NodeList object, and that same value must always be returned, unless this element is an input element whose type attribute is in the Hidden state, in which case it must instead return null.

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#dom-lfe-labels

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: Clarify when the "labels" attribute of <input> is null

items.content_html:
Description

This updates the parts of the WebGL best practices page that were called out in #26597:

  • Estimate a per-pixel VRAM budget: the three steps were written inline as "1) … 2) … 3)", so I turned them into a proper list. I also removed the line saying mobile devices usually have smaller screens. In device pixels that's no longer true, since a lot of phones have as many pixels as a laptop or desktop display, or more.
  • Memory usage of depth and stencil formats: added a short note on why this matters in practice. It feeds into your VRAM estimate, and it means a combined depth-stencil attachment usually costs no more than a 24-bit depth-only one.
  • devicePixelRatio and high-dpi rendering: now points to ResizeObserver with device-pixel-content-box as the main approach. Pre-snapping stays as a fallback, with a note that it doesn't work when the canvas is sized by its container.
  • ResizeObserver and 'device-pixel-content-box': replaced the promise-based getDevicePixelSize() example with the more common pattern of setting the canvas size inside the observer callback. It falls back to contentBoxSize * devicePixelRatio when devicePixelContentBoxSize isn't available (Safari doesn't support it yet). It also handles browsers that throw on the unknown box option.

Motivation

Some of the advice was outdated or didn't hold up. The old example also made an app wait on a promise before it knew the canvas size, which isn't how most WebGL apps handle resizing.

Additional details

  • I ran the new example in Chromium at a device pixel ratio of 1.5. A canvas with a 353.9 × 233.7 CSS box got a 531 × 351 drawing buffer, matching its device-pixel size. I also forced the fallback path (no devicePixelContentBoxSize, and observe() throwing for the box option), and it still sized the canvas correctly.
  • Support info for devicePixelContentBoxSize comes from BCD.
  • I left the "Use texStorage to create textures" section alone. The issue says texSubImage2D uploads are slower than texImage2D in Chrome, but I couldn't confirm that's still the case, so I'd rather leave that one to someone who knows.
  • markdownlint, Prettier, cspell and the front-matter linter pass. A local rari build of the page reports no flaws, and the new in-page links resolve.

Related issues and pull requests

Relates to #26597 (covers everything in it except the texStorage point)
items.title: WebGL best practices: fix VRAM budget advice and update canvas sizing guidance

items.content_html:
Description

As per mdn/mdn#822, the Tools and setup section of the learning area is outdated and repeats content available elsewhere on MDN. It is also a maintenance burden — quite a few parts of it would be better updated so they point to the tool manufacturer's docs rather than us repeating it.

This PR updates the Tools and setup section to fix this problem. The following list provides notes on what I've done for each article in the section:

  • What software do I need to build a website?: This stuff is covered in Installing basic software, so I've removed it and redirected to there.
  • How much does it cost to do something on the web?: Some of this stuff was useful; I've put those bits in Publishing your website and deleted it and redirected to there. I also restructured the "Publishing your website" guide and updated the gh pages info there, pointing to GitHub's docs where appropriate and adding guidance in between. It's a shame there isn't one simple GitHub guide to follow to easily get something on gh-pages.
  • What text editors are available?: Covered in Installing basic software. Deleted and redirected to there.
  • What are browser developer tools?: This is still genuinely useful. I've copyedited it to improve the text and bring a few things up to date, and crunched the images a bit to reduce file size.
  • How do you make sure your website works properly?: This is a bit of a strange mishmash of debugging tips. The bit about the network inspector and HTTP statuses was quite useful and not covered anywhere else, so I've added a brief network inspector section that covers it to What are browser developer tools?, then deleted it and redirected to there.
  • How do you set up a local testing server?: This is genuinely useful and linked to in a few places. I've given it a copy edit and improved a few things.
  • How do you upload files to a web server?: Another article that covers publishing web content. Again, consolidated, deleted, and redirected to Publishing your website
  • How do I use GitHub Pages?: It is not worth us maintaining a separate page on github pages. I've deleted this and redirected to the Version control module page. I've made sure that page includes a prominent link to the gh pages step by step on "Publishing your website".
  • How do you host your website on Google App Engine?: This was already deleted and redirected to the Google App Engine docs, so I've just removed the link from the section landing page.
  • What tools are available to debug and improve website performance?: already removed and redirected to the relevant dev tools documentation, so I've just removed the link from the landing page.

There are only two articles left in the "Tools and setup" section now, so maybe a future PR could look at restructuring further.

Motivation

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes mdn/mdn#822
items.title: Consolidate Tools and setup Learn section content
